column1: # Per-shot parity gate thresholds for tools/parity/compare.ps1 -Gate.
# Format: name <TAB> min_ssim <TAB> max_mean_abs_diff [<TAB> min_world_ssim]
# The fourth column is optional. It is the **world-band** SSIM floor: compare.ps1 also scores each
# pair with the port's HUD band (bottom 22 % of the crop) removed from both sides, which separates the
# renderer/HUD term from the world's own parity (round 103: the HUD is worth 0.07-0.09 on a level-1
# pair). A row that names it is parity-checked on that number, with the full-frame floor left as a
# gross-breakage check; a row without it gates on the full-frame number alone. No row uses it yet:
# none of the ungated pairs is rescued by the world-band score.
# These are tolerances, not equality: retail (1997 D3D via dgVoodoo2, or software) and the port
# (Bevy) are different renderers, and the port's HUD is inside its frame while the retail world
# crop has none. A *verified* pose pair currently scores 0.62-0.63 SSIM here (0.69-0.71 world-band),
# so the floors sit just under that: a real camera or draw regression is caught (moving the level-1
# eye by 0.03 units drops the pair to ~0.24), while renderer/HUD noise is not.
# Raising a floor is the right move when a renderer change improves a pair; lowering one needs
# a reason in the commit message. A pair captured without a row here is reported as UNGRADED.
# The numbers are tied to the capture policy in tools/parity/port-capture.ps1: 600 frames
# (`--frames 600`), the window sized from the retail sidecar, and whatever renderer
# retail-capture.ps1 used (16-bit D3D via dgVoodoo2 by default). `--shot` runs step the
# simulation by a fixed 1/60 s (`CaptureDt`) so 600 frames are exactly 10 s of game time,
# which is the moment the retail side's capture represents; a wall-clock step made the same
# command measure a different amount of play on every machine. Changing either side's
# framing or frame count invalidates the numbers.
# route_catwalk and route_door are captured but intentionally not gated. The port now warps the
# player to the row's pose (`--warp`, the same pose retail's `warp` gives its body), so scripts and
# AI see a body there — but retail's reference in these two rooms is **red from damage tint**: the
# body is being damaged (level 1's door: health 100 -> 44 over the series; catwalk: 100/100 ->
# 81/11) and `sithActor_DamageActor` adds `damage * 0.04` red to the player's palette tint
# (`sithPlayer_AddDynamicTint`, decaying 0.4/s). Both halves of that layer are ported now (state and
# draw), and the world-band score confirms the residual is content, not the HUD: the two rows move
# by only +0.04 when the HUD band is removed, because retail's reference is a *saturated* tint at
# ~10 s while the port's capture is still at a different point in the fight (AI engagement, step 5).
